cells.side: monergist-leaning member (ELCA; the PCUSA's Reformed confessions stand on the same side)
cells.document: Augsburg Confession (a confessional standard of the ELCA under its Confession of Faith)
cells.excerpt: But it has no power, without the Holy Ghost, to work the righteousness of God, that is, spiritual righteousness
cells.shows: The Lutheran confession held by the ELCA says the human will cannot produce saving righteousness without the Holy Spirit.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (one side of a genuine split; the 50 is a midpoint between this and the Wesleyan cell below)
cells.binding: Confessional standard of the ELCA; not binding on the PCUSA or UMC

cells.document: The Articles of Religion of the Methodist Church (in The Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church 2020/2024)
cells.date: 1784 (Wesley's abridgement; adopted by American Methodism 1784, fixed 1808)
cells.excerpt: without the grace of God by Christ preventing us, that we may have a good will, and working with us, when we have that good will
cells.shows: The United Methodist standard teaches that grace goes before every good act of the will and then works together with the will so freed.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (the other side of the split; grace first, then cooperation)
cells.binding: Doctrinal standard of the UMC, protected by its Restrictive Rules; not binding on the PCUSA or ELCA

cells.document: The Use of the Means of Grace: A Statement on the Practice of Word and Sacrament (ELCA)
cells.excerpt: the crucified and risen Christ is present, giving his true body and blood as food and drink
cells.shows: The ELCA teaches that Christ is really present in Holy Communion and gives his body and blood there.
cells.binding: Adopted 'for guidance and practice' by the ELCA Churchwide Assembly; copyright 1997 ELCA, so link only

cells.document: The Articles of Religion of the Methodist Church
cells.excerpt: they are certain signs of grace, and God's good will toward us, by which he doth work invisibly in us
cells.shows: The United Methodist standard denies that sacraments are only badges of profession and says God works through them.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (sacramental, though Article XVIII speaks of partaking 'with faith' and is less explicit on presence than the Lutheran text, so marginally weaker than 5 for the UMC taken alone)

cells.document: Guidelines: The UMC and the Charismatic Movement (Resolution #8015, The Book of Resolutions of The United Methodist Church 2020/2024; #8010 in 2008)
cells.section: Guidelines for all; concluding section on discernment
cells.excerpt: to be aware of and to respond to manifestations of the Holy Spirit in our world today
cells.shows: The UMC General Conference tells members to seek the Spirit's gifts and to stay open to manifestations today, while requiring order, interpretation of tongues and careful discernment.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (open but cautious continuationism, matching a moderate 35 rather than a Pentecostal score)
cells.binding: General Conference resolution: official UMC guidance, not a doctrinal standard; representative of, not binding on, the PCUSA and ELCA. No comparable ELCA or PCUSA document was opened.

cells.document: Eschatology: The Doctrine of Last Things. Twelve Theses and a Position Paper (Presbyterian Church in the U.S., a PCUSA predecessor; published by the PCUSA)
cells.date: 1978 (118th General Assembly, PCUS), reaffirming the 1944 PCUS General Assembly report on dispensationalism
cells.section: Assembly action 3; section I.C.4; Appendix: Report on Dispensationalism (1944 GA)
cells.excerpt: reaffirm the 1944 General Assembly, PCUS, position regarding dispensationalism
cells.shows: The Assembly reaffirmed its 1944 finding that dispensationalism is out of accord with the Westminster standards, while stating this was no criticism of premillennialism as such.
cells.binding: Adopted 'for guidance and study in the church' by a predecessor body; hosted by the PCUSA (landing page https://pcusa.org/resource/eschatology-doctrine-last-things). Copyright 1978, so link only. The 1944 wording ('out of accord with the system of the doctrine set forth in the Confession of Faith') was read at https://www.pcahistory.org/documents/pcus1944.html

cells.side: qualification within the same pole, not an opposite side
cells.document: A Theological Understanding of the Relationship Between Christians and Jews (PCUSA)
cells.excerpt: has been engrafted into the people of God established by the covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
cells.shows: The PCUSA describes the church as grafted into the one people of God and adds in the same affirmation that Christians have not replaced Jews.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports, with a caution: it fits 'one people' but rejects supersessionist wording, so site copy for this tradition should not say the church replaces or simply inherits from Israel
cells.binding: Commended to the church for study and reflection as a provisional understanding; not a confessional standard. PCUSA's own copy: https://pcusa.org/sites/default/files/christiansjews1.pdf (not opened; the ccjr.us copy was read)

cells.document: The Articles of Religion of the Methodist Church
cells.section: Article V, Of the Sufficiency of the Holy Scriptures for Salvation
cells.excerpt: whatsoever is not read therein, nor may be proved thereby, is not to be required of any man that it should be believed as an article of faith
cells.shows: The United Methodist standard holds that nothing may be required as an article of faith unless it can be proved from Scripture.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports the Scripture-alone half of the 55; taken alone it would sit further toward Scripture alone than 55

cells.document: Our Theological Task (The Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church 2020/2024)
cells.date: Adopted 1972, rewritten 1988; text as in the 2020/2024 Discipline
cells.excerpt: revealed in Scripture, illumined by tradition, vivified in personal experience, and confirmed by reason
cells.shows: United Methodists name Scripture as primary and read it with tradition, experience and reason as working guides, none of them infallible alongside it.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (Scripture primary with a real but subordinate role for tradition explains a near-centre 55 rather than a high score)
cells.binding: Part of the Discipline but expressly not a doctrinal standard; the 1972 and 1988 dates are from general knowledge of the Discipline's history and were not stated on the page opened, so verify before printing them. Copyright United Methodist Publishing House, so link only

cells.document: The Use of the Means of Grace: A Statement on the Practice of Word and Sacrament (ELCA)
cells.section: Principle 35 (see also Application 7A on the lectionary and church year)
cells.excerpt: Lutheran congregations celebrate the Holy Communion every Sunday and festival. This confession remains the norm for our practice.
cells.shows: The ELCA names weekly Communion on Sundays and festivals as its norm and commends the Revised Common Lectionary and the church year.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports for the ELCA; likely stronger than 25 taken alone, since PCUSA and UMC practice is more varied. No PCUSA Directory for Worship or UMC Book of Worship passage was opened, so the 25 for the whole family is only partly documented
cells.binding: Adopted for guidance and practice by the ELCA; copyright 1997, so link only

notes: This entry is a family of three denominations with different confessional bases, so no single document binds all three; every cell names which body owns the document. Grace is a genuine split (Lutheran and Reformed confessions against Wesleyan prevenient grace), so one document per side is given and the audited 50 is a midpoint, not a shared teaching. All excerpts were checked verbatim against the page or PDF text opened on 2026-09-19 (umc.org pages and the bookofconcord.org and ccjr.us pages by raw HTML; the two PDFs by pdftotext). The ELCA PDF is a scan with OCR, so stray spaces before punctuation in the source were closed up in the excerpts; wording is unchanged. In the ELCA Principle 35 excerpt a footnote marker after 'Augsburg Confession' falls outside the quoted words. Gaps: no PCUSA Book of Confessions passage was opened for grace, table or authority (the PCUSA hosts it as a large PDF; the confessional Presbyterian entry may already cite Westminster), no ELCA or PCUSA statement on spiritual gifts was found, and no PCUSA or UMC worship directory was opened. The 1944 PCUS report is quoted only in the binding field from a PCA Historical Center transcription, not from PCUSA's own site.
